source_snapshot.procedure: Generic setup says clear logs; open Dashboard and Server Health > Sensor Reading.
source_snapshot.criteria: Sensor reading and threshold are human readable and match specification.
source_snapshot.deepseek: YES treats symbolic 1~N as one sensor, cannot discover N or prove population coverage, assumes ordinary thresholds on a likely discrete status family, and truncates the inventory.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION correctly requires discovery-first enumeration and vendor state decoding. V3.1 additionally binds each status channel to module/rotor/controller/header/redundancy zone and distinguishes discrete status fields from RPM, PWM, tach and temperature.

old_problem: N is an unresolved platform population variable, not a runnable range. A fan module may expose multiple rotors or one composite status, optional positions may be absent, and discrete event states may have assertion masks rather than numeric thresholds. Guessing N as 16 from a conflicting physical-removal case would reduce or distort coverage.
disposition_reason: Define canonical N from the approved fitted module/rotor inventory, generate the exact expected status-record set, and validate every discrete raw state and both UI views without fault stimulus. Preserve applicable/not-applicable field semantics and explicitly disposition optional/unfitted channels. The Project inventory/state dictionary is an execution prerequisite, not an unresolved review decision.
decision_basis: XLSX row 904, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, selection manifest, separate physical-removal case, RPM/thermal context and preserved V3.1 record were directly reviewed.
The separate dynamic case's `1~16` and temperature/status contradictions supply no authority for this passive row's N and remain outside its scope.
Fan status is normally discrete/composite coverage: numeric threshold fields may be not applicable and must not be fabricated to satisfy generic Criteria.

ED-09 assigns physical fan handling to humans, ED-13 governs optional/unfitted N/A, ED-15 requires the approved state dictionary, ED-17 preserves logs and ED-20 requires every discovered identity to remain separate.

test_case.test_name: Verify every inventory-defined STATUS_FAN channel without fan manipulation
test_case.purpose: Verify the complete Project-installed fan status set is present and correctly displayed in Dashboard and Server Health, with canonical N derived from platform inventory and every channel mapped to its fan module/rotor/controller/header/zone and decoded according to the approved discrete-state definition and freshness rule.
required_package: Chassis/fan-board/BMC/SDR build and approved fitted fan-module/rotor population establishing canonical N
Expected exact STATUS_FAN names and mapping to physical module, rotor, slot, controller/header, thermal zone and redundancy group
Stable SDR number/name/sensor type/event-reading type/entity instance and corresponding API/Dashboard/Server Health identity
Explicit applicability of numeric threshold fields and mapping to separate RPM/tach/PWM/temperature sensors where relevant
BMC polling cadence, UI propagation/freshness tolerance and current unchanged fan policy/mode
Validated protected read-only BMC/browser client and pinned immutable reviewed `sensor.git` revision/checksum or approved manual method
test_case.test_command: Do not clear SEL, fan, thermal or BMC logs and do not stop/remove/reseat a fan, obstruct airflow, change PWM/policy, inject a fault, alter thresholds or power-cycle. Build the authoritative expected channel set and N from chassis inventory; never send `STATUS_FAN 1~N`, infer N from another case or count rotors/modules interchangeably. Enumerate the complete SDR/API repository, resolve every exact status record and review the Script before use. Capture stable identity, raw event bits/masks, decoded state, field applicability and timestamp plus matching Dashboard and Server Health visual rows. Compare with the approved topology/state/freshness rules and stop without retry on missing, duplicate, swapped, stale or divergent channels.
test_case.expected_result: The discovered exact channel set equals the Project expected set and establishes N. Every applicable raw status and both UI views agree on physical module/rotor/controller/zone identity, approved decoded state and freshness. Optional/unfitted channels follow the specified absence behavior; non-applicable numeric thresholds are recorded as such rather than invented. RPM, temperature, dynamic removal and fault behavior remain separate coverage.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires authoritative canonical N, one explicit result for every expected status channel, complete raw/two-UI identity/state/freshness evidence and engineer acceptance under the vendor discrete-state map. A literal 1~N query, first-100-line fallback, summary health, count, guessed N, RPM value or fabricated numeric threshold cannot pass. Missing/extra/duplicate/swapped/stale identity, incorrectly decoded bits, unexpected absent/degraded/failed state or UI mismatch is FAIL. Missing topology/state definitions or reviewed interface is NOT READY, not Pending or PASS; physical fan fault/recovery is outside this row.
safety_gate: Preserve SEL, fan, thermal and BMC history; do not execute the generic clear-log step.
Derive N from approved inventory and enumerate exact records; do not import 16 from the separate conflicting case or omit optional fitted hardware.
Keep presence/status distinct from RPM, PWM, tach and temperature; mark unsupported threshold fields not applicable only when the sensor definition proves it.
Do not stop/remove/reseat fans, block airflow, change PWM/policy, inject faults, alter thresholds or power-cycle.
Do not truncate output, expose credentials, assume a cipher or run an unreviewed Script; no automatic retry.
expected_evidence: Chassis/fan-board/BMC identity and approved module/rotor population establishing N
Complete per-channel module/rotor/slot/controller-header/zone/redundancy plus SDR/API/UI identity matrix
Separate full raw discrete state, assertion/deassertion masks, decoded state, field applicability and synchronized timestamp for every channel
Dashboard and Server Health visual rows plus recorded fan policy/polling/UI propagation and mapped corroborating RPM only where defined
Preserved logs, no-fault/no-fan-or-airflow-or-policy change/no-retry proof, final cooling/BMC health and all-channel engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: No mutation is expected. On unknown N/topology/state bits, missing or stale records, or unexpected cooling/BMC health, stop and preserve original evidence and fan policy. Obtain the approved inventory and event-state specification and continue only with read-only diagnostics; do not manipulate a fan to resolve ambiguity. Any separately authorized physical fault test requires human handling and its own thermal safety/recovery plan.

source_conflict.reason: Within this row, Items, passive UI Procedure and Criteria consistently target fan status presentation. The N/1~16 and temperature/status conflicts belong to a separate physical-removal source case.

blocked.reason: The passive all-installed-status objective and safe discovery method are complete. Platform inventory and the discrete-state definition can bind N and acceptance without a fault.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Canonical fitted module/rotor inventory and exact N, per-channel physical/controller/SDR/UI map, discrete masks/state/latch/absence definitions, threshold applicability, polling/freshness rules and protected reviewed method.
pending.execution_status: NOT STARTED; READ ONLY; NO FAN, AIRFLOW, PWM, POLICY, FAULT, THRESHOLD OR POWER CHANGE; SCRIPT NOT APPROVED

external_authorities.title: Master-referenced internal sensor Script
external_authorities.application: Pin and review before use; it cannot define canonical N, physical topology, discrete event semantics or acceptance.

project_authority: Platform fan topology/redundancy specification, fitted inventory, BMC SDR/event-state definition, fan-controller documentation and WebUI schema define N and the PASS/FAIL state map.
